items.excerpt: Trump touts his power at Kentucky rally to energize voters ahead of midterm elections HIGHLAND HEIGHTS, Ky. (AP) — President Donald Trump is emphasizing his influence during his second term at a rally in Kentucky. He claimed on Saturday that he could achieve "unbelievable" things, citing his decision to change how the U.S. government refers to the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. Trump was in Highland Heights to support Republican candidates, including Ed Gallrein for the U.S. House. As midterm elections approach, Republicans face challenges, with high living costs and frustration over Trump's administration affecting voter sentiment. Trump warned that a Democratic win could reverse his policies. Vance faces tough questions on Iran war, immigration and more in CBS town hall WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Vice President JD Vance faced tough questions from voters about the Trump administration’s policies on data centers, high costs, immigration and his own rhetoric in a town hall on CBS News that aired Saturday night. The string of sharp queries, some from voters who said they had supported him and President Donald Trump, previewed the rocky path he may face trying to answer for the administration’s record if he runs for president himself. Major fire breaks out in Alberta after deadly incident at Canadian military base EDMONTON, Alberta (AP) — Canada’s defense minister says that people have been killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire, while reports said that large numbers of injured people were being transported to hospitals. Fire crews scrambled late into the night Saturday as fierce winds whipped flames beyond Canadian Forces Base Wainwright and into the surrounding rural area. It was not immediately clear how many people were killed or injured, but a doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, 120 miles northwest, told Canada’s national broadcaster that patients were being brought to hospitals across the city as health-care facilities around the base became “completely overwhelmed” by the number of people needing care. Blaze at St Petersburg oil sites as Kyiv launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia Ukrainian attacks have set an oil export terminal ablaze in St. Petersburg. Kyiv launched over 1,000 drones across Russia in one of its largest aerial bombardments. The attack comes amid tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. One person was killed and five were wounded in the attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city’s Ruchi oil depot. Meanwhile, one woman died and at least two other people were injured after Russia launched two attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said. Pope returns to Vatican days after surgery; surgeon says he should be fit for Latin America tour VATICAN CITY (AP) — The surgeon who removed Pope Leo XIV's cancerous tumor says there are “no clinical reasons” to prevent the pontiff from traveling to Latin America next month. Vatican media reported this after the pope returned to the Vatican from the hospital. Dr. Stefano Margaritora told Vatican News that the pope is expected to recover fully from surgery in about 10 days. Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seen WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump’s abrupt decision to waive sanctions on Russia is drawing outrage and concern from members of Congress. Trump's move came late Friday, two days before the penalties were scheduled to take effect. Republican Sen. Thom Tillis says Trump's move is “beyond irresponsible.” Lawmakers had overwhelmingly passed the legislation in a bipartisan display of U.S. support for Ukraine. Trump signed it into law last month. The waiver is the latest instance of Trump drawing the U.S. closer to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump recently announced a diesel deal with Putin to import Russian energy in hopes of curbing high gas prices in the U.S. that are roiling the midterm elections. Masked settlers attack European diplomats in the occupied West Bank JERUSALEM (AP) — Masked settlers attacked a group of European diplomats in the occupied West Bank, a French mayor who was struck and others say. The attackers targeted Belgium’s consul general and French and Polish diplomats on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said. The French mayor described the attack by men with metal bars. Israel’s military condemned the attack as a “severe act of violence,” and police said they had opened an investigation. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned against “premature conclusions.” At least four people have been killed since the olive harvest began in the Palestinian territory earlier this month, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. ... Hurricane Trudy strengthens to Category 2 as it approaches Mexico coast MIAMI (AP) — The U.S. National Hurricane Center says Trudy has strengthened to a Category 2 hurricane as it moves toward Mexico’s southwestern and west-central Pacific coast. A hurricane warning was in effect Saturday from Manzanillo in Colima state to Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco. The latest NHC data showed the Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 kph) and was about 175 miles (280 kilometers) south of Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco state and 100 miles (160 kilometers) south-southwest of Manzanillo, moving northwest at 10 mph (17 kph). Meanwhile, Typhoon Champi strengthened into a Category 4 Super Typhoon as it moved toward Guam.

items.excerpt: Retail price impacts from the Iran war are uneven but add up for US households before midterms NEW YORK (AP) — High fuel prices are making it more expensive to drive, fly and buy some goods more than seven months into the U.S.-Iran war. That's prolonging the strain on American households as the midterm elections approach., The chief economist at Moody’s Analytics estimates the war has cost the average U.S. household the equivalent of almost $2,000, including $1,100 related to energy. Motorists and airline passengers so far have borne the clearest consequences from disrupted Middle East oil shipments. The elevated cost of making and moving goods hasn't translated into across-the-board retail price increases. Shoppers may not be spared indefinitely, though. U.S. consumers are uneasy about the increasingly high-tech ways that restaurant chains and major retailers are setting prices. Digital price tags are replacing paper ones in grocery aisles. Artificial intelligence tools help businesses decide what to charge by predicting how customers might respond. Terms like “dynamic pricing” and “surveillance pricing” are stirring up anger and anxiety on social media. Much of the concern focuses on whether customer data is getting used to give different people different prices for the same product. Walmart and McDonald's say critics misunderstand how their pricing tools work. Lawmakers and regulators are taking preemptive action to restrict when companies can use personal data in pricing. BANGKOK (AP) — U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says he won't prejudge what the U.S. central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings. However, he repeatedly vowed to “deliver price stability.” Warsh spoke Friday on the sidelines of a meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. The global surge in prices is a key concern of the financial leaders meeting. Stubbornly high U.S. inflation is expected to lead the Fed to raise its key interest rate in coming months after a rate hike in September.

items.title: Powered by spikes in energy prices, inflation surges to 3.7% - NKyTribune
items.excerpt: “Inflation has wiped out wage gains for 6 months now,” Heather Long, the chief economist for Navy Federal, wrote in a social media post. “It’s a financial squeeze. Americans are trying to work more hours to make up for it, but many are still falling behind.” Spikes in energy prices were largely responsible: Gas is now up 34% for the year, and fuel oil, which includes diesel, is up 72% as the Iran war drags on. States including Georgia, Kentucky, Illinois, Indiana, North Carolina, Ohio and Utah have enacted gas tax relief measures recently to battle rising prices. North Carolina expects to lose more than $362 million in tax revenue for the fiscal year because of a gas tax holiday. New York state estimates fuel oil prices are up 67% from last year, with home heating oil at $6.21 a gallon as of this month. Connecticut announced plans Oct. 13 for additional state aid for home heating assistance, partly because of high prices for delivered oil. Other than energy, the largest factor was food away from home, up 3.5%. The only decreases were medical care products, down 3.3%, and used cars and trucks, up for the month but still down 1.5% for the year. So-called “core” inflation outside of volatile food and energy was a more modest 2.6%. Stateline reporter Tim Henderson can be reached at thenderson@stateline.org. (AP) — President Donald Trump touted his power in his second go around in the White House Saturday while rallying in Kentucky to bolster Republican turnout as his party struggles in the midterms, saying, "I can do stuff that is unbelievable.” Trump, who spoke in the city of Highland Heights to boost Republican candidates including Ed Gallrein for the U.S. House, was riffing on his decision to change how the U.S. government refers to the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America. “I don’t think I could have done this in my first term. This is a much more powerful term,” Trump said. “Google wouldn’t have taken my call in the first. Now, they kiss my ass." ... “Well, I also changed the name of a lake in Canada to the Lake America," he continued, referring to Lake Ontario. Trump's self-proclaimed power is set against voter frustration with how he's wielded it, with tariffs and the Iran war driving up prices and more Americans seeing the president looking out for his own interests and not those of the country. Vance faces tough questions on Iran war, immigration and more in CBS town hall WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Vice President JD Vance faced tough questions from voters about the Trump administration’s policies on data centers, high costs, immigration and his own rhetoric in a town hall on CBS News that aired Saturday night. The string of sharp queries, some from voters who said they had supported him and President Donald Trump, previewed the rocky path he may face trying to answer for the administration’s record if he runs for president himself in 2028. Vance, who said during the town hall there's “of course” a chance he doesn't run for president, faced an especially pointed question about “a failure of leadership” posted by the widow of one of six U.S. soldiers killed by an Iranian drone strike in Kuwait, which occurred the day after Trump started the war with Iran. “This literally is the first time I’ve heard of this,” Vance said in response. ... Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. He left the hospital on Saturday, well ahead of the week-long hospital stay the Vatican had initially anticipated. Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seen WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's abrupt decision to waive sanctions on Russia days before they were to take effect drew outrage Saturday from members of Congress, which had overwhelmingly passed the legislation in a bipartisan display of American support for Ukraine in the war with Russia. Lawmakers from both parties blasted the executive order late Friday, the latest in a series of steps that the Republican president has taken drawing the United States closer to Russia's Vladimir Putin. Trump recently announced a diesel deal with Putin to import Russian energy in a long-shot effort to curb high gas prices in the U.S. that are roiling the midterm elections on Nov. 3.

items.excerpt: What To Watch On TV And Streaming Sunday, October 18, 2026 # What To Watch Sunday: Vampire Diaries Vet Joins Tracker, Simpsons Goes Slasher, New Marshals, And More By Nick Caruso Oct. 18, 2026 3:00 am EST Every day, TVLine's What to Watch column spotlights new and returning English-language shows (and select movies) premiering or airing fresh episodes across broadcast, cable and streaming — organized below by release time and alphabetically within each slot. On TV this Sunday: Michael Malarkey visits "Tracker," a serial killer stalks "The Simpsons," and a drone crash causes chaos on "Marshals." ## Showtimes for October 18, 2026 ### Saturday Night Live UK Peacock James Norton hosts; The Streets performs. 8:00 PM ET ### Amish Revenge Lifetime MOVIE PREMIERE A widowed Amish mother (Boti Bliss) takes in a handsome young man (Brigdon York) who claims to be homeless, only to discover that he isn't who he says he is. ### Mr. & Mrs. Christmas Hallmark Channel MOVIE PREMIERE A holiday display expert (Brendan Penny) relocates with his children to a quaint town, where reviving its Christmas Market brings him together with a practical accountant (Pascale Hutton) hoping to prove she's ready for a new leadership role. ### Professor T PBS **Season 5 premiere**: Jasper's new relationship is put to the test when a mysterious death arouses his suspicions. ### The Real Housewives of Potomac Bravo Karen celebrates her return home with a party theme that no one can decode; Gizelle tries to restore her friendship with Tia. ### The Simpsons In a new "Treehouse of Horror" episode, all hell breaks loose on Halloween when a killer comes to Springfield and hacks their way through town. 8:30 PM ET ### Animal Control Frank goes undercover at Roman’s new privatized animal control company, Pax Romana. ### Marshals The Marshals are sent to track three Broken Rock residents accused of shooting down a military test drone; tensions rise between federal authorities and tribal leadership after the drone crash takes the life of a Broken Rock member. ### American Hostage Fred wrestles with selling the false immunity agreement to Tony over the air, taking the story back to 1972. ### Maigret **Season 2 premiere**: Maigret investigates a young woman's death, putting himself directly in the path of people who will do anything to keep the truth hidden. ### The Pet Cemetery Murders Detectives make strides in Dorothy’s case, and an unlikely witness comes forward with a vexing admission; details emerge about Dorothy's struggles with addiction and the mysterious deaths of her past husbands. ### Universal Basic Guys Darren becomes a summer camp lifeguard; Mark and Hank get into magnet fishing. 9:30 PM ET ### Grimsburg Stan breaks bad to help Dr. Pentos sell illegal candy to students at the middle school; Flute mentors Otis for his first undercover operation. ### Tracker Colter gets hired to track down a woman who disappeared after an argument with her husband in a deserted Texas town; an unexpected reunion with an old friend (Michael Malarkey), leaves Reenie revisiting her past. ### The Gold **Season 2 premiere**: The police chase the other half of the stolen Brink's-Mat gold when it resurfaces; in Tenerife, John Palmer's successful timeshare business starts to attract unwanted attention. ### Treasure Island Onboard the Hispaniola, Bess targets Graham for protection as Long John lays the groundwork for mutiny with the crew; when violence erupts, Jim makes a calculated move that shifts the balance, tipping the scales in Long John's favor. ### Youth After getting asked out on a date, Alex tries to make sense of where things stand with Patrick; as Ruari starts his internship at the agency, Sam and Alex attempt to win back Malcolm before Grayson swoops in.

The self-described perfectionist who spent two years on "Lux" talks with correspondent Seth Doane about her mix of classical, opera and pop, and her almost spiritual commitment to her craft, defined by what she calls "a search for communion."

items.title: Tini: FUTTURA World Tour | Miami & Miami Beach
items.excerpt: ### Oct 18, 2026 ##### Doors open: 7:00 PM | Show starts: 8:00 PM ... Argentine pop artist Tini brings her FUTTURA World Tour to downtown Miami for the tour’s only U.S. stop. Tini: FUTTURA World Tour takes place Sunday, October 18, 2026 at Kaseya Center. The tour is described as a retrospective project spanning Tini’s different musical eras, from her early international breakthrough on Disney Channel Latin America’s Violetta to her solo career in pop, urbano, cumbia and alternative pop. The Miami concert follows the tour’s launch in Buenos Aires and brings the arena production to a U.S. audience for one night only. Born Martina Stoessel, Tini is an Argentine singer, actress and performer whose albums include Tini, Quiero Volver, Tini Tini Tini, Cupido and Un Mechón de Pelo. Her career includes chart success in Latin America and Europe, multiple major music awards and collaborations that have expanded her reach across Latin pop and global music audiences. The event is open to all ages, though ages 18 and older are recommended.
